title: TSMC Shares Fall 6.4% in AI Selloff as Chipmaker Plans New 3nm Tainan Fab
summary:
TSMC shares fell 6.4% on Thursday amid a broader selloff in Asian tech and AI stocks, even as the chipmaker unveiled plans for an additional 3nm fab in Tainan, Taiwan, slated for production in the first half of 2028. The company also targets 2028 mass production for its next-generation A14 node and expects capital expenditure over the next three years to exceed the past three, while maintaining its 2026 capex guidance at $60 billion to $64 billion after spending $13.84 billion in the third quarter.

Across its global footprint of roughly 20 fabs under construction, TSMC completed building its second Arizona plant for third quarter 2027 mass production ahead of schedule and will bring 3nm technology to its second fab in Kumamoto, Japan, in 2028. However, the steep ramp-up of 2nm chips, which rose from 3% to 8% of wafer revenue in the third quarter, trimmed gross margin by 1.3 percentage points sequentially to 66.4%. Management projected fourth quarter gross margin of 65% to 67%, with overseas fab expansion diluting full-year 2026 gross margin by 2% and by 3% to 4% in later years.

The stock drop followed TSMC's sixth consecutive quarter of record net profit, which rose 68.7% year over year to NT$763.1 billion ($23.7 billion) on revenue of $46.72 billion and earnings of $4.60 per ADR. The company guided fourth quarter revenue to $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, above the $50.5 billion consensus estimate, as CEO C.C. Wei said AI demand shows no sign of slowing, accelerator revenue growth will likely top its prior mid-to-high 50% compound annual target through 2029, and there is "no ceiling" on TSMC's profitability.

selectedTweets.text:
$TSM released earnings today. I was more curious about commentary given recent the market panic.

For analyst Q&A rounds: 

Q: Citi explicitly challenged TSMC on AI financing, HBM, CoWoS, lasers and the risk of overbuilding capacity 

A: $TSM assessed CSP capex, DC construction conditions, customer financial conditions, and supply of critical components. 

Management's conclusion is still that "demand exceeds supply". As well as that AI accelerator revenue growth could exceed its previous 50%+ CAGR projection through 2029.

This is a more meaningful statement since it addresses some concerns regarding recent selloff. 

Q: JPM asked if wafer supply could be tighter in 2027 than in 2026 (demand visibility)

A: Wei (Chairman/CEO) stated $TSM even sends staff to verify DC construction progress on site. And after assessing all the factors, TSMC believes gap between supply and demand remains substantial.  

It could not determine whether the extent of the gap given customers continues to increase demand. 

Q: On pricing power:

A: Wei responded that there is "no ceiling on TSMC's profitability" but that profits will not surge dramatically overnight.

(Source: NextApple, Taiwanese press)

Regarding earnings, very strong: as usual 

- TSMC record profits of $23.6B (68% Y/Y growth), and revenue jumping to $46.72B, beating expectations.

- Q4 Guidance was $52.3-$54.3B revenue off 65-67% gross margins.

TLDR:

- No signs of any slowdown or collapse as AI demand far exceeds supply for foreseeable future. $TSM is probably the fundamental proxy/canary to how the overall AI semi trade is doing. 

- On financing concerns and fear of overcapacity showing up in semiconductor demand: 

$TSM specifically examined the risks investors are concerned about now and assessment still points to unmet demand. 

During the Q&A session, Wei said AI demand was "very, extremely strong," with absolutely no signs of slowing.

Underlying AI semi supply chain growth is healthier than recent market panic suggest.
